out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS PROVIDED PIC WITH THE FAIRFAX COUNTY VOMIT AND DIARRHEA CLEAN UP PROCEDURES. PLEASE RETAIN FOR FUTURE INSPECTIONS.

violations.title: Cleaning Procedure
violations.observation: Observed staff rinse hands under running water after handling Raw chicken
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wash their hands and exposed portions of their arms by: 1) discarding used gloves; 2) rinsing under warm running water; 3) applying soap; 4) rubbing together for at least 10-15 seconds; 5) rinsing thoroughly under warm running water; and 6) drying with paper towels or air drying device. EHS INSTRUCTED STAFF TO WASH HANDS WITH SOAP AND HOT WATER. STAFF WASHED HANDS WITH SOAP AND HOT WATER AND USED A PAPER TOWELS TO DRY HANDS. RE-TRAIN STAFF ON WHEN TO WASH HANDS. SEE WHEN TO WASH FACT SHEET.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Paper towels were not observed at the hand sink by the 3-compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. PIC PLACED A ROLLER OF PAPER TOWELS AT THIS HAND SINK. ALL HAND SINKS MUST HAVE PAPER TOWELS TO FACILITATE PROPER HAND WASHING.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed the handsink at the BY THE ENTRANCE OF THE KITCHEN being used TO WASH AN EMPLOYEE’S CUP
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCONTINUE USING THE HAND SINK FOR DISH WASHING. PIC REMOVED SPONGE HOLDERS FROM THE HAND SINK. PIC INSTRUCTED STAFF TO WASH ALL EMPLOYEE DISHES AT THE 3-COMPARTMENT SINK.

violations.title: Separation of Clean and Soiled Equipment/Utensils
violations.observation: Observed staff wear purple rubber gloves mix a large container of Raw chicken with his gloved hands. Without removing gloves, staff open the bulk bins of dry goods.
violations.corrective_action: Foods shall be prepared using only cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils to prevent contamination to the foods being prepared. EHS INSTRUCTED STAFF TO TAKE OFF GLOVES BEFORE RETRIEVING OTHER INGREDIENTS. PIC WASHED AND SANITIZED THE LIDS OF THE BULK BINS.

violations.title: Equipment Clean to Sight and Touch
violations.observation: Encrusted grease deposits and/or other soil deposits were observed on the food contact surfaces of the following cooking equipment: 1) sides of deep fryer
violations.corrective_action: The food-contact surfaces of cooking equipment and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. MORE ROUTINE CLEANING OF THE EXTERIOR OF THE DEEP FRYER IS REQUIRED.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Observed bag of onions being stored on the floor of the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. ELEVATE ALL FOOD OFF OF THE FLOOR TO FACILITATE PROPER AND FREQUENT CLEANING. CORRECT BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: plastic to-go containers and cans being stored directly in the bulk containers of salt, flour, rice, etc.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. REMOVE PLASTIC TO-GO CONTAINERS AND CANS. REPLACE WITH SCOOPS WITH HANDLES. STORE SCOOP ON THE OUTSIDE OR IN THE INGREDIENTS WITH ITS HANDLE STICKING UPWARDS TO AVOID CONTAMINATING THE FOOD. CORRECT BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION. CHOPSTIX (Inspection Date: 03/19/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Soiled Linens Properly Stored
violations.observation: Observed heavily stained towels being used in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Soiled linens shall be kept in clean, nonabsorbent receptacles or clean, washable laundry bags and stored and transported to prevent contamination of food, clean equipment, clean utensils, and single service items. PIC DISCARDED THE TOWELS AND TOOK OUT CLEAN TOWELS TO USE. DISCARD TOWELS WHEN HEAVILY SOILED AND STAINED.

violations.title: Equip/Utensils Self-Draining Position/Covered/Inverted
violations.observation: Observed food storage containers and mixing bowls that have been cleaned not stored covered or inverted.
violations.corrective_action: Clean equipment and utensils shall be stored covered or inverted to prevent contamination. INVERT ALL CLEANED AND SANITIZED CONTAINERS IN STORAGE. CORRECT BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: 1) sides of ALL coolers; 2) handles of ALL coolers; 3) doors of ALL coolers; 4) tops and sides of rice cookers; 5) top interior panel of rice cookers; 6) exterior of soup warmers; 7) exterior of ALL bulk bins
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. CLEAN ALL AREAS BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Premises Free of Litter
violations.observation: Observed maintenance tools, unused pots, and unused kitchen knives being stored throughout the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Remove all litter from the premises to allow for regular and effective cleaning and to prevent harborage conditions. REMOVED ALL UNUSED ITEMS IN FROM THE KITCHEN. CONSOLIDATE EQUIPMENT AND SUPPLIES TO REDUCE HARBORAGE CONDITIONS AND TO FACILITATE PROPER AND FREQUENT CLEANING. CORRECT BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION.

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed the following areas of the kitchen floor encrusted with food debris and grime: 1) under prep table; 2) under coolers; 3) under shelves; 4) under 3 compartment sink and next to drain
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. CLEAN ALL AREAS BY THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: 1) Raw pooled eggs were observed being stored about prepared vegetables in the 2DR prep top wok line; 2) cooked chicken was observed being stored under Raw chicken in the walk- in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC MOVED THE EGGS TO A LOWER SHELF OF THE COOLER. PIC MOVED THE PAN OF COOKED CHICKEN TO THE TOP SHELF ABOVE RAW CHICKEN.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Chlorine Requirements
violations.observation: When prompted, PIC opened a new bottle of bleach and mixed it with water to used as sanitizer. When tested using PIC’s chlorine test kit and EHS’s chlorine test kit, concentration was 0ppm. Odor from the new bottle of bleach had a faint smell of chlorine.
violations.corrective_action: A chlorine-based sanitizing solution shall have a minimum concentration of at least 50 to 200 ppm total chlorine when tested using the appropriate test kit. PIC INSTRUCTED STAFF TO BUY BLEACH FROM A NEARBY STORE. PIC MIXED NEWLY PURCHASED BLEACH WITH WATER. CONCENTRATION WAS OBSERVED BETWEEN 50-200ppm.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: 1) multiple containers of portioned brown rice being stored in the 2DR glass slide cooler. Upon discussion with PIC, rice will be kept for 4 days and then discarded.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC DATE MARKED THE RICE. USE OR DISCARD WITHIN 6 DAYS.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Durable Materials
violations.observation: Observed multiple plastic take-out bags being used to store food throughout the coolers and freezers.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. PIC MOVED THE FOOD INTO REUSABLE FOOD STORAGE CONTAINERS.

violations.title: Equipment Clean to Sight and Touch
violations.observation: Observed accumulated dirt, food debris, grease and oil on the exterior of all of the coolers; on the interior of the coolers specifically under the prep top lids and shelving; exterior of the 3 soup warmers and 2 rice warmers; exterior of 5 gallon soy sauce containers.
violations.corrective_action: The food-contact surfaces of cooking equipment and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. CONTINUE TO CLEAN ROUTINELY.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Observed no written Employee Health Policy or Employee Illness Agreement on site.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS EMAILED THE CHINESE VERSION OF THE FAIRFAX COUNTY EMPLOYEE ILLNESS AGREEMENT TO PIC. PLEASE HAVE EACH STAFF MEMBER READ AND SIGN A COPY OF THIS DOCUMENT. RETAIN THESE ON SITE FOR FUTURE INSPECTIONS.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: Observed no written vomit and diarrhea policy on site.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS EMAILED THE CHINESE VERSION OF FAIRFAX COUNTY’S VOMIT AND DIARRHEA CLEAN-UP PROCEDURES TO PIC. PLEASE RETAIN THIS DOCUMENT FOR FUTURE INSPECTIONS.

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: Observed PIC not wash his hands after changing tasks during the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO WASH HIS HANDS AFTER CHANGING TASKS. HANDS MUST BE WASHED FREQUENTLY TO PREVENT CROSS CONTAMINATION. SEE WHEN TO WASH HAND OUT. CHOPSTIX (Inspection Date: 04/10/2025) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Poison/Toxic Material, Conditions of Use
violations.observation: Pesticides labeled for residential use were observed in the facility and are being applied by the operator to control pests. EHS observed a can of Hot Shot home use pesticide being stored in the facility.
violations.corrective_action: Remove residential use pesticides from the facility. When necessary for pest control, chemical pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination. PIC DISCARDED THE CAN OF PESTICIDE. EHS DISCUSSED THAT HOME USE PESTICIDES ARE NOT ALLOW IN PERMITTED FOOD FACILITIES. PLEASE CONTACT A LICENSED PEST CONTROL OPERATOR FOR PEST CONTROL SERVICES.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Observed empty cans and to-go containers being stored bulk bins of salt, sugar, rice, corn starch, etc.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO REMOVE ALL CANS AND CONTAINERS FROM BULK STORAGE BINS TO PREVENT CROSS CONTAMINATION. SCOOPS WITH HANDLES CAN BE STORED IN THE BULK BIN WITH ITS HANDLE STICKING UPWARDS.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Durable Materials
violations.observation: Observed cooked chicken wings and other ready-to-eat food being stored in plastic take-out bags.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.
